_about: People who have shaped the Spokane tech community, researched from public sources 2026-10-02. Professional, public facts only, each with its sources. These are editorial entries, not user profiles: nobody here signed up, and nothing here says whether anyone is looking for work.

people.name: Adam Parish
people.summary: Spokane-based design engineer working across product design, design systems and React/TypeScript. Lead Product Designer at fintech company Atomic since 2022, previously at Aon, and co-founder of XpenseOne (2014–2018).
people.note: Self-published on his own site; no independent press coverage found.

people.name: Tom Simpson
people.role: President, Spokane Angel Alliance · CEO, Ignite Northwest
people.summary: Longtime Spokane venture investor. Founded Northwest Venture Associates in 1986, has led the Spokane Angel Alliance since 2008, runs the Kick-Start seed funds, and co-founded etailz. As CEO of the nonprofit accelerator Ignite Northwest he oversaw the sale of the Spokane Technology Center to WSU.

people.name: Connor Simpson
people.summary: Spokane entrepreneur who co-founded the secondhand-clothing marketplace Barters Closet after Spokane's first Startup Weekend, and later co-founded Weddings By Owner, an 'Airbnb for weddings' launched in Spokane with Jordan Allen.
people.note: No current role found in a citable source.

people.name: Jordan Allen
people.summary: Serial Spokane founder. Built Stay Alfred past $100M in revenue before its 2020 shutdown, sold the real estate bidding platform Doorsey to Auction.io in 2023, and in 2024 launched BuyWander in Spokane Valley. A Spokane Journal of Business 2026 Person of Influence.

people.name: Fred Brown
people.summary: Spokane AI entrepreneur who founded conversational AI pioneer Next IT in 2002 and sold it to Verint in 2017. Has since launched Omniscia AI, building AI representatives for businesses in regulated industries.

people.name: Lisa Shaffer
people.summary: Spokane genetics entrepreneur. Co-founded Signature Genomic Laboratories in 2003 and sold it to PerkinElmer for $90M in 2010, then founded Paw Print Genetics in 2012, acquired by Neogen in 2021.
roles: Founder and CEO, Paw Print Genetics (2012–2021)

people.name: Kim Zentz
people.summary: Spokane technology and civic-innovation leader who helped form the smart-city nonprofit Urbanova in 2016 and led it until 2021, after a career spanning Avista Labs, Innovate Washington, Spokane Transit and WSU's urban-innovation work.
roles: Director of urban innovation, Washington State University

people.name: Tyler Lafferty
people.summary: Co-founder, with Nick Murto, of the Spokane digital agencies Seven2 and 14Four, which have made work for national clients including Disney, Expedia and AT&T.

people.name: Josh Neblett
people.summary: Co-founded etailz in Spokane in 2008 and grew it from a college business plan into a $100M-revenue e-commerce company, sold to Trans World Entertainment for $75M in 2016. Stepped down as CEO in 2019 and has since left Spokane.

people.name: Bernard Daines
people.role: Founder, Packet Engines and World Wide Packets
people.summary: Gigabit Ethernet pioneer who moved from Silicon Valley to Spokane and founded Packet Engines, sold to Alcatel in 1998, and World Wide Packets, sold to Ciena in 2008. He died in 2021.
